glosses: to capitalize
обращать в капитал, капитализировать
kapitalizować, skapitalizować (np. odsetki)
transitiv:
eine Ausgabe als Investition verbuchen

examples.text: Diese 10.000 € hier können wir auch kapitalisieren, schließlich ist es für ein Wirtschaftsgut, das lange halten soll.

glosses: etwas verwerten, in Geld umwandeln

examples.text: Aus dem Handel kapitalisierten drei Millionen Euro.

glosses: sein Geld anlegen
mit großen Buchstaben schreiben

examples.text: Man kann mit einem Shortcut kapitalisieren, das geht ganz einfach und wandelt erst den Anfangsbuchstaben und bei zweimaligen Drücken das ganze Wort in Großbuchstaben um.

glosses: berechnen des Gegenwartswertes wiederkehrender künftiger Zahlungen durch deren Diskontierung

examples.text: Könnten Sie bitte diese Mieteinnahmen kapitalisieren? Mich interessiert es doch, in wie weit wir hier eine Sicherheit für einen Kredit haben.

glosses: To exchange for cash.

examples.text: The gamblers cashed in their remaining chips at the end of the night.

Some nights, I stay up cashing in my bad luck
Some nights, I call it a draw

glosses: To settle one's debts, accounts, or bills, especially relating to gambling.

examples.text: He's just mad because I haven't cashed in yet.

glosses: To profit from something; to take advantage of an opportunity in order to profit, especially financially; to capitalize on.

examples.text: Lots of people tried to cash in on that market, but few succeeded.

Showman Monte Proser tried to cash in on the boom on a mass basis with his Dance Carnival in Madison Square Garden, where dancers lindy hopped, shagged and fox-trotted to the orchestras of Benny Goodman, Larry Clinton and Charlie Barnett[…]
For all PSG's attacking riches, it was Manchester City who carried the more concerted threat - with the only concern initially that they could not cash in on their domination.

glosses: To die.

examples.text: He turned to me, and "Cap," says he, "I'll cash in this trip, I guess; / And if I do, I'm asking that you won't refuse my last request."[…
Well, it all ended up, I lost my privileges for two weeks. But someday before I cash in, I hope to make it in the straw.

glosses: In writing or editing, to write (something: either an entire word or text, or just the initial letter(s) thereof) in capital letters, in upper case.

examples.text: In German, all nouns are capitalized.

glosses: To contribute or acquire capital (money or other resources) for.

examples.text: Some states require proof that a new venture is properly capitalized before the state will issue a certificate of incorporation.
To have any hope of success a new venture must be properly capitalized.

glosses: To convert into capital, i.e., to get cash or similar immediately fungible resources for some less fungible property or source of future income.

examples.text: If we obtain a loan using the business as collateral, the effect will be to capitalize our next ten years of income, giving us cash today that we can use to buy out our competitor.

glosses: To treat as capital, not as an expense.
To profit or to obtain an advantage.

examples.text: The home team took several shots on goal but was unable to capitalize until late in the game.

glosses: To seize, as an opportunity; to obtain a benefit from; to invest on something profitable.

examples.text: The home team appeared to have the advantage throughout the game, and finally capitalized on their opponents' weakness with just two minutes remaining, scoring several points in quick succession.
